LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – TRICKSTER STORIES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Trickster stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Trickster stories, part of Strand 8 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are trickster narratives shared in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work collaboratively to collect varied trickster narratives from the community,

2. organise the collection of trickster narratives in a class portfolio,

3. brainstorm characters often portrayed as tricksters in oral narratives,

4. conduct a reader’s theatre to read the trickster narrative in the class portfolio,

5. listen to a resource person narrate a trickster story,

6. compose a summary of the trickster narrative listened to,

7. outline the characters and plot in a trickster narrative,

8. work collaboratively to stage a creative skit on a trickster narrative,

9. brainstorm the moral lessons addressed in trickster narratives.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work collaboratively to collect varied trickster narratives from the community,
2. organise the collection of trickster narratives in a class portfolio,
3. brainstorm characters often portrayed as tricksters in oral narratives,
4. conduct a reader’s theatre to read the trickster narrative in the class portfolio,
5. listen to a resource person narrate a trickster story,
6. compose a summary of the trickster narrative listened to,
7. outline the characters and plot in a trickster narrative,
8. work collaboratively to stage a creative skit on a trickster narrative,
9. brainstorm the moral lessons addressed in trickster narratives.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Trickster stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner displays respect and acceptance of heterogeneity when working

collaboratively with peers to collect varied trickster narratives from the community.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is developed as the learner brainstorms the moral lessons addressed in

trickster narratives.

Values:
• Integrity: This is developed as the learner exhibits commitment to duty when working collaboratively with peers to

stage a creative skit on a trickster narrative.

• Peace: This is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance when brainstorming characters often portrayed as tricksters in

oral narratives, with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion is developed as the learner collaboratively engages in reading, analysing, and presenting trickster stories to

the class.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concepts learnt when exploring trickster stories to their learning of narratives in English and

Kiswahili.
